The Conservative Commitment to Government 'Closest to the People' Is a Texas-Sized Scam
The Conservative Commitment to Government 'Closest to the People' Is a Texas-Sized Scam
Meanwhile, in Arizona, we have another tragic case of Republican honesty.
By
Charles P. Pierce
Published: Mar 11, 2021 5:03 PM EST
23
Gabriella Demczuk
//
Getty Images
(Permanent Musical
Accompaniment
To This Post)
Being our semi-regular weekly survey of what’s goin’ down in the several states where, as we know, the real work of governmentin’ gets done, and where there’s a wicked wind blowing on that upper deck.
One of our favorite stops on this semi-regular weekly survey are those places where the conservative dedication to the notion that the government “closer to the people” is always preferable is revealed to be the scam that it is. Generally, this happens when a state decides to do something contrary to what the national conservative establishment believes. But now, in Texas, we have a conservative governor and attorney general knuckling the city government of the state’s capital city. From the
Austin American-Statesman
:
Undaunted, Austin Mayor Steve Adler said he and Travis County Judge Andy Brown
will continue enforcing the safety mandates
.  "We will fight Gov. Abbott and Attorney General Paxton’s assault against doctors and data for as long as we possibly can," Adler said, adding that wearing masks is one of the most effective methods of slowing the spread of COVID-19. The conflict is the latest pandemic dust-up between Democratic local leaders and Republican state officials. In a letter sent Wednesday afternoon to Adler and Brown, Paxton said Abbott's most recent executive order, which ended a statewide mask mandate and prohibited limits on business operations, must be followed because it "has the force and effect of state law and supersedes local rules and regulations.”
You have to love an assertion of the
Eric Cartman Principles of Federalism
when applied by an AG who also happens to have spent time under both investigation and indictment, as well as being sued by Twitter. From the
Texas Tribune
:
Twitter’s suit comes as Paxton faces a series of other legal issues, including claims of abuse of office and bribery. Former aides allege the attorney general used his power to assist an Austin real estate developer with legal matters after he helped Paxton remodel his house and employed a woman with whom Paxton allegedly had an affair. The whistleblowers’ allegations have reportedly
sparked
an FBI investigation. Four of the former aides claim they were fired in retaliation for telling authorities they believed Paxton had done illegal favors for a political donor and are suing. During a
March 1 whistleblower hearing
, which Paxton did not attend, lawyers representing his office argued Paxton is not a public employee and
cannot be sued under the Texas Whistleblower Act
. The attorney general has previously dismissed the claims against him as “false allegations” from “rogue employees.”
And this is the guy who’s suing the mayor of Austin for declining to help the state of Texas get people sick again. C’mon, Texas. Honest to god.
We move along to Arizona, where the national pandemic of Saying The Quiet Part Loud has claimed another victim. From
CNN
:
"There's a fundamental difference between Democrats and Republicans," Kavanagh said. "Democrats value as many people as possible voting, and they're willing to risk fraud. Republicans are more concerned about fraud, so we don't mind putting security measures in that won't let everybody vote -- but everybody shouldn't be voting.”
Another tragic case of Republican honesty.
NBC NewsWire
//
Getty Images
Governor Asa Hutchinson’s sincere and long-held convictions are going to cost Arkansas taxpayers.
We double-back to Arkansas, where the anti-choice people  have concocted another law aimed at the new conservative majority on the Supreme Court. From
CNN
:
The Arkansas
bill
, SB6, bans providers from performing abortions "except to save the life of a pregnant woman in a medical emergency," and makes no exceptions for instances of rape, incest or fetal anomalies. Those found to violate the law could face a fine of up to $100,000 and up to 10 years in prison. "I will sign SB6 because of overwhelming legislative support and my sincere and long-held pro-life convictions," Arkansas Gov. Asa Hutchinson, a Republican, said in a statement. "SB6 is in contradiction of binding precedents of the U.S. Supreme Court, but it is the intent of the legislation to set the stage for the Supreme Court overturning current case law.”
Of course, the Arkansas taxpayer will end up paying to defend this blatantly unconstitutional law all the way up to the Supreme Court where, admittedly, anything can happen at this point. But one wonders how Republicans,
who now are on record as being against helping people during the pandemic
, will find the political safe space also to chuck the privacy rights of 51 percent of the population overboard. But I’m sure we’ll hear a lot about how we should just leave this issue to “local government,” which can’t be trusted to mandate face masks.
And we conclude, as is our custom, in the great state of Oklahoma, where Blog Official Chuck Wagon Entertainer of the Year Friedman of the Plains brings us the curious tale of how the state legislature has legalized vehicular homicide. From the
Tulsa World
:
Debate went late into Tuesday and voting happened early Wednesday morning as the Oklahoma House approved a bill that would grant immunity to drivers who hit protesters. Rep. Kevin McDugle, R-Broken Arrow, said House Bill 1674 was inspired
by a May 31, 2020, incident where Black Lives Matter protesters blocked Interstate 244 in Tulsa
. A pickup pulling a horse trailer drove through the crowd, sending two people to the hospital. During bill questioning, Rep. Regina Goodwin, D-Tulsa, reminded House colleagues that
a man fell from I-244 and broke his neck and back
during the incident, and that the driver reportedly showed protesters a gun before driving through the protesters on the interstate.
But making you wear a mask is an impossible infringement of basic human freedom. Conservatism is a weird room.
This is your democracy, America. Cherish it.
